title: Late Breaking Results: Less Sense Makes More Sense: In-Sensor Compressive Learning for Efficient Machine Vision
problem: High-resolution image sensors generate excessive data requiring quantization and transmission overhead, consuming energy inefficiently for downstream deep learning tasks.
motivation: Conventional sensor-to-processor pipelines incur high energy cost in data acquisition and transmission; in-sensor compression is needed to reduce this bottleneck.
method: Instead of sending raw high-resolution images to a computer, this approach embeds a compression algorithm directly in the image sensor. The algorithm uses a 1-bit encoder (compressing each pixel value down to 1 bit, essentially binary information) that learns which visual features matter for your specific task. The encoder and the downstream deep learning task are jointly optimized together during training, so the sensor learns what details to keep and what to discard for that particular job. This shrinks the data right at the source, eliminating the energy cost of transmitting unnecessary image data.
key_novelty: A 1-bit encoder embedded in the image sensor and jointly optimized with the downstream vision task achieves 10× data compression while maintaining task accuracy.
contributions: In-sensor compressive learning framework that integrates 1-bit encoder within image sensors
Joint optimization between encoder and downstream vision tasks for task-specific compression
10× data compression with minimal (1.6% maximum) accuracy loss and 3.93× energy savings at sensor
Outperforms prior in-sensor and on-device compression methods
limitations: Limited evaluation scope; practical integration with standard image sensors and scaling to higher resolutions not discussed.
primary_theme: in-sensor compressive learning for efficient vision
